newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, January 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, January 30.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The Constitutional Court will make its pronouncement today on the validity of 30 proposed referendums, ranging from abolishing the residual element of proportional representation to decriminalising the use of marijuana. The Court is reportedly set to turn down most of them (all).

* The cabinet will meet today to discuss a government decree including cheap loans and grants to dairy farmers hit by EU fines. Milk producers have staged two weeks of protests to press their demands (all).
* A mafia turncoat has been arrested on charges of pushing drugs, refuelling a fierce debate on the treatment the Italian state grants to turncoats (all).

*Prime Minister Romano Prodi said he was not worried about the lira and denied he had said the currency had become too strong. The lira fell on Wednesday to 985 against the mark and to 1,626 against the dollar (all).
*Information technology group Olivetti reported a pre-tax loss for 1996 around 800 billion lire while its annual sales fell 16 percent to 8.27 trillion lire (all).
*The board of telecom holding Stet will meet today to ratify the nomination of Guido Rossi as chairman and Tomaso Tommasi di Vignano as managing director (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
